sources.title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

items.statement: An extended-real sigma-strongly convex function plus a convex function is sigma-strongly convex for sigma > 0.
items.conditions: Retain the original effective-domain semantics; neither summand is assumed proper. An empty intersection of effective domains is not excluded.
items.reuse_hypothesis: Generic addition interface, then exact source recovery.

items.statement: For a nonempty convex subset C of a Euclidean space, one half of the squared norm plus the indicator of C is 1-strongly convex.
items.conditions: Retain nonempty and convex C; the indicator takes the value positive infinity outside C.
items.reuse_hypothesis: Combine the existing quadratic identity with the new addition interface; exercise a nonsmooth extended-real consumer.

items.statement: For nonnegative alpha and beta, alpha f1 + beta f2 has strong-convexity parameter alpha mu1 + beta mu2 on Q1 intersect Q2.
items.conditions: Both functions are continuously differentiable in the source sense and use the same norm. Preserve alpha=beta=0 using the source convention S_0^1=F^1; do not silently require a positive resulting parameter.
items.reuse_hypothesis: Share nonnegative curvature arithmetic and explicitly recover the differentiable formulation.

items.statement: If f belongs to S_mu^1 on the whole finite-dimensional space and its gradient vanishes at x_star, f(x) >= f(x_star) + (mu/2) norm(x-x_star)^2 for every x.
items.conditions: Preserve the arbitrary norm and whole-space domain. The stationary point is an assumption; existence is not a conclusion of this item.
items.reuse_hypothesis: Expose and consume a stationary quadratic-growth interface.

items.statement: For a proper convex extended-real function on a real Hilbert space, beta-strong convexity with beta > 0 implies beta-strong monotonicity of the subdifferential.
items.conditions: Do not add lower semicontinuity or differentiability. Preserve the subgradient graph and extended-real effective domain.
items.reuse_hypothesis: Use the shared quadratic inequality to obtain an operator interface.

items.statement: A monotone operator A is beta-strongly monotone iff its resolvent is (beta+1)-cocoercive; consequently the resolvent is 1/(beta+1)-Lipschitz.
items.conditions: beta > 0. The resolvent domain is ran(Id+A). Do not assert it is all of H without maximal-monotonicity evidence. Preserve both directions and the Lipschitz conclusion.
items.reuse_hypothesis: An operator consumer uses the preceding strong-monotonicity interface.

derived_bridge.label: derived synthesis, not an additional textbook theorem
derived_bridge.scope: Whole finite-dimensional real inner-product space; C1 real-valued f; positive mu; real-to-EReal embedding. Relate the existing StrongConvexC1On and StrongConvex predicates without narrowing either original source interface.
derived_bridge.background: StrongConvexC1On.iff_strongConvexOn and strongConvex_iff_strongConvexOn already exist; the connecting theorem and source recoveries do not yet exist.

reserve.reason: Existence and uniqueness need closedness, properness and coercivity; do not replace with an assumed minimizer.
Needs Lipschitz-gradient and cocoercivity background, including mu=L boundary.
Algorithmic consumer after mixed gradient inequality; preserve step-size interval and full rate.

execution: Serial on the retained three-source project, each batch statement preparation, library integration and proof; do not start from disjoint projects.
selection_policy: Keep every selected item and failure; record dependency reuse, source recovery and independent clients separately. No selection changes based on method outcomes.
materials_publication: Bibliographic locators and original paraphrases only; no textbook PDF or extracted pages included.
